capability_boundaries.boundary: Core owns the base gate mechanics (transferability, real anchors, real stakes, non-template openers, character-specific voice detection, blocking conditions, rewrite priorities). CW bolt-on extends application scope to fiction prose and adds an 11-item fiction naturalness standard. CW does not fork or reimplement any base check.
capability_boundaries.fail_closed_behavior: If both Core and CW attempt to define contradictory rewrite priorities for the same detection, composition fails closed.

capability_boundaries.boundary: Core owns PCR candidate marking, PCR promotion ratification requirement, and pcr_ratification_link semantics. CW bolt-on owns the twenty-section fiction PCR content schema and the writing-specific explicit-command-only trigger. Any CW-declared PCR promotion still requires Core-owned user ratification.
capability_boundaries.fail_closed_behavior: If CW attempts to mark pcr-promoted without pcr_ratification_link, Core Governor blocks silently-promoted PCR (Class 0).

capability_boundaries.boundary: Core owns registration schema and prohibited fields (bypass/exemption/override/gate_suppression). CW bolt-on adds writing-phase-mode entries under the same schema; each inherits every gate unconditionally per Core's gate-inheritance rule. CW cannot amend Core registry entries or grant bypass to any registered mode.
capability_boundaries.fail_closed_behavior: If a CW mode-registry entry contains a prohibited field (bypass/exemption/override), composition fails closed at bolt-on load.

capability_boundaries.boundary: Core owns Non-Interference Invariant (§21.1), reconstruction inputs (§21.4), reconstruction acceptance standard (§21.5), and failure behavior table (§21.6). CW bolt-on owns fiction-specific trigger classifications and continuity-repair rules that consume Core recovery outcomes.
capability_boundaries.fail_closed_behavior: If CW recovery declares acceptance under criteria weaker than Core §21.5, composition fails closed.

capability_boundaries.boundary: Core owns CREATE/EDIT/REVIEW modes, canonical-source rule, delta discipline, preservation rule, regression check, repair rule, source-code mental model. CW bolt-on owns fiction-specific editing/critique/preservation-checkpoint/conversion protocols that use Core editing mechanics.
capability_boundaries.fail_closed_behavior: If CW attempts to permit editing from memory when a canonical artifact exists (Core §Canonical Source Rule), composition fails closed.

capability_boundaries.boundary: Core defines a Tier-2 binding position (`extension-contract.tier2-user-profile-attachment`) and reserves user-response, user-voice-style, and user-editing-preference categories for Tier 2. Core does not silently absorb user-specific content. Tier-2 package is not built in this task; the reserved binding position ensures future attachment does not require Core redesign.

Core defines a Tier-3 binding position (`extension-contract.tier3-project-attachment`). Tier 3 owns project canon, project instructions, project decisions, PCR/continuation state, project-specific artifacts. Tier 3 may not escalate authority above Core, Tier 2, or applicable bolt-on.
